Use the supplied portrait as visual reference for face and hair: retain its softly tapered facial outline, large dark eyes, natural lip shape, and short dark bob with wispy fringe. The main figure is a fictional adult stage performer whose invented role and circumstances belong to this photograph. Inside an old opera dressing room between the final rehearsal and the opening stage call, she pauses the hurry to return a borrowed silver flower brooch to her colleague. The performer stands in the foreground, her weight settled over her rear leg, wearing a sleeveless smoke-gray satin stage gown with a softly defined waist. Her colleague stands to the right, holding a folded rehearsal schedule in the left hand and pausing with the right hand open just beyond the brooch. definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities.
